newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa adds gains in afternoon, ends higher.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa adds gains in afternoon, ends higher.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures added to slim morning gains to end firmly in positive ground on Thursday.
July closed up 12 stg at 1,032 stg per tonne but still failed to pierce and end above resistance at 1,035. September gained 10 to end at 1,048.

Volume was moderate at 5,275 lots. July was most active, trading 1,562 contracts. December and March 1998 each tallied more than 1,000 lots. Fewer than 900 lots changed hands in each of the other months.
Traders attributed some of cocoa's gains to spillover from surging coffee prices. July robusta coffee leapt to more than a 20-month high on tight supply and Brazil frost fears.
Sterling's move above $1.64 and 2.79 marks on European economic and monetary union (EMU) nervousness also aided London cocoa.

EMU jitters surfaced after the Bundesbank renounced on Wednesday the German government's plans to revalue its assets, including gold. That boosted sterling's safe-haven status because the UK is not committed to the single currency plans.

Despite cocoa's gains, traders said July was still stuck in a range between about 1,035 and 1,000. Only if July can sustain gains above 1,035 and convincingly break 1,060 will more attention shift from the frenzied buying spree in coffee to cocoa.
In options, no contracts changed hands again.
